finding.claim: /admin/drop never enforces the 'dba' role. The Authorize() result is discarded, so any authenticated user can run DROP TABLE.
finding.source: Any caller who reaches /admin/drop with a request context containing a *User (api.go:22, 25). Roles are not checked because the error is ignored.
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + ...) at api.go:27, a destructive DDL operation on the database.

trace.note: /admin/drop is registered with dropTable and no wrapper or middleware.
u := userFrom(r) takes the user from the request context.
Authorize(u, "dba") is called, but its error return is not checked. Compare vacuum at api.go:33-36, which returns 403 on error.
runSQL executes DROP TABLE regardless of the authorization outcome.
The handler returns 204 whether or not the user had the role.

finding.guards_checked: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is correct on its own, and vacuum uses it properly. In dropTable, the call's result is discarded, so it does nothing. No middleware, mux wrapper, or role check appears elsewhere in the repo.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is the only role check. It is called at api.go:26 but its error return is discarded, so it has no effect. No middleware or wrapper in the repo: /admin/drop is registered directly with dropTable at api.go:44. The only other effective control is in vacuum (api.go:33-36), which is not on the drop path.
verdict.reason: At api.go:26 the Authorize(u, "dba") error is discarded, so dropTable reaches runSQL("DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t")) at api.go:27 for any user object in the request context, and the route at api.go:44 has no other guard. The attacker needs only an authenticated low-privilege user, since the code that sets the context user is not in this repo, and runSQL here is a no-op stub.

finding.claim: SQL injection: the 't' parameter is concatenated into a DDL statement without validation or quoting.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27. This reads the URL query or the form body, so any HTTP client can set it.
finding.sink: runSQL at api.go:27, which executes the concatenated string as SQL.

trace.note: The route is reachable over HTTP on :8083 (api.go:46).
r.FormValue("t") is concatenated directly into "DROP TABLE " with no allowlist, identifier quoting, or regex check.
The result is passed to runSQL, which is a stub here; the real driver and whether it allows stacked statements are not visible in this repo.

finding.guards_checked: No validation, escaping, or parameterization on the path. The only gate in front of it is the broken Authorize check from F1, so it's reachable by any authenticated user. Even after F1 is fixed, a legitimate DBA can still inject into this statement.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize (api.go:13-20) is the only candidate control, but dropTable calls it as a bare statement at api.go:26 and discards its error, so it never blocks anything. No parameterization, identifier quoting, or allowlist exists on the path at api.go:27. The route is registered at api.go:44 and served on :8083 at api.go:46.
verdict.reason: The "t" value from r.FormValue at api.go:27 is concatenated into "DROP TABLE " and passed to runSQL, while the role check at api.go:26 is a bare call whose error is discarded, so any authenticated user can reach the injection. The sink runSQL is a stub at api.go:41, so the actual execution behavior is outside this repo, but the concatenation itself is confirmed.

finding.claim: userFrom does an unchecked type assertion. A request without a *User under the "user" key panics instead of being rejected.
finding.source: The request context. Nothing in this repo sets the "user" key, so whether it is set depends on middleware that is not in this repo.
finding.sink: The type assertion .(*User) at api.go:22, which panics on nil or wrong type. It is called first in both handlers (api.go:25, 32).

trace.note: Both routes are registered with no authentication wrapper in this file.
userFrom(r) runs before any role check.
r.Context().Value("user").(*User) panics if the value is nil or of another type.

finding.guards_checked: No nil check or comma-ok form. net/http recovers panics per request, so the server keeps running. The failure is closed, not open, because the handler stops before any SQL runs. Severity depends on whether authentication is applied elsewhere.

verdict.guard_found: Implicit: the unchecked assertion at api.go:22 panics before runSQL (api.go:27, 37) is reached, and net/http recovers the panic per request (library behavior, not in this repo), so the failure is fail-closed. No explicit nil or comma-ok check exists.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (api.go:22 panics, routes at api.go:44-45 have no auth wrapper, userFrom runs before any check at api.go:25 and 32), but a nil or wrong-type context value makes the handler panic before any SQL runs, so an unauthenticated request gets no privileged effect; the result is a failed request, not an authorization bypass. The real issue nearby is that dropTable ignores Authorize's error at api.go:26, which is a separate finding and only matters if middleware sets a "user" value.

finding.claim: Possible CSRF on the state-changing /admin/drop endpoint. It accepts any HTTP method and reads parameters from the URL query, not only the POST body.
finding.source: A cross-site request from a victim's browser, if the session is carried by cookies. The attacker controls the query string through a link or image.

trace.note: r.FormValue merges URL query and body, so a GET with ?t=... works.
The route has no method check and no CSRF token.

finding.guards_checked: No method restriction and no CSRF token. Whether this is exploitable depends on how the session is carried, which is not visible in this repo. Conditional, and it applies only when combined with F1 or with a legitimate DBA.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is a bare statement, so its error return is discarded and it blocks nothing. No method check or CSRF token exists on the route (api.go:44). The only other check, the vacuum handler's `if err := Authorize(...)` at api.go:33, is not in the dropTable path. The session mechanism that populates the "user" context value (userFrom, api.go:22) is not in this repo.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: r.FormValue at api.go:27 accepts query parameters and the route at api.go:44 has no method or token check, but the CSRF claim depends on whether the session is cookie-based, which is set outside this repo (userFrom, api.go:22). The real defect is more serious and confirmed by the code: the Authorize call at api.go:26 discards its error, so any authenticated user (not only a DBA) can reach runSQL("DROP TABLE ...") at api.go:27 without CSRF. Report that as a missing-authorization finding, and keep this CSRF claim conditional on the session design.
